prospect.name: Ryan
prospect.occupation: Cultural support worker for a non-profit, connecting Indigenous people with Indigenous culture and ceremony. Largely office-based. Also holds a part-time job and runs two further projects plus a personal project — six commitments in total.
prospect.family_status: Recently separated — breakup one week before the call. One son, just turned 17, a basketball player. Lives with a roommate.
prospect.training_background: Sedentary for years — 'I've been on the couch for years' — and restarted roughly two to three months ago after his then-partner began going to the gym. Currently two to three sessions a week counting ceremony work: gym circuits of 30 lb farmer's carries and 40 lb suitcase carries plus steady-state jogging and walking, around 75 minutes. Physical ceremony work involves Zercher-lifting 75 lb logs, hauling rocks and wood in extreme heat. Did parkour as a young man and was in very good shape then. Trained with a bodybuilder friend years ago and responds well to training. No real kettlebell experience. Preparing for Sundance from 26 July to 4 August — four to six hours of dancing a day for four days without food or water.
prospect.medical: Generalised joint hypermobility, self-described as double-jointed — hyperextends shoulders, elbows and knees, and reports his knees do not feel solid, requiring conscious muscle control over foot placement when running. Fell roughly seven feet from a rolling scaffold about seven years ago, landing base-first on concrete, displacing a vertebra; a chiropractor also identified one hip sitting higher than the other. Ongoing back problems — his back locks up when inactive. Reports chronic daily headaches and 'crippling pain every day'. Mental health conditions disclosed at the end of discovery: recurrent depressive episodes and manic episodes. Family history of fatal heart attacks in the men of his family; his father's discs are degenerating and his mother uses a wheelchair. Formerly homeless and formerly used drugs, both in the past — 'my body has been through a lot of a lot. There's probably a bunch of micro injuries that I wouldn't be able to name'. Self-reports BMI as poor. Cut out near-daily ice cream and most sugar around two months ago.

signals: Lost substantial ground across a hard decade — homelessness, drug use, years of survival mode and sedentism at 278 lb
Wants a former self back and names it: 'back when I was a kid, like, I used to do parkour... I was in very good shape'
Carries visible regret: 'I've been treating myself like I don't love myself. And that's just the facts, man'
Trigger is mortality and a recent breakup rather than optimisation — around ten people close to him died last year
Distinguished from the_prehab_fighter because there is no single active health event driving this; the conditions are chronic and long-standing

goals.text: Build sustainable functional strength rather than isolated gym strength — not the guy who can push four plates but struggles running upstairs
Have the stamina and endurance to get through his days without crashing
Be physically capable for ceremony work — Sundance dancing four to six hours a day for four days without food or water, plus lifting logs and hauling rocks
Longevity and capability into his sixties, unlike the elders in ceremony who struggle to stand, and unlike his parents
Learn kettlebell skills well enough to pass them on to his 17-year-old son, who is already injuring himself in basketball
Be alive and well for his son's future children
Lose belly fat, fill out his chest and arms, and look and feel stronger
Develop self-assuredness and a relationship of self-love with his own body
Do things still on his list — summits, parasailing, skydiving, and learning kung fu in the mountains in his sixties

pains.text: Generalised joint hypermobility with knees that do not feel solid, requiring constant conscious control of landing and foot placement
Displaced vertebra from a seven-foot fall onto concrete about seven years ago, plus uneven hip height; back locks up when he is inactive
Chronic daily headaches and what he describes as crippling pain every day
Recurrent depressive and manic episodes; gets severely depressed when sedentary
Sedentary for years at 278 lb with declining muscle mass and a fear of it accelerating with age
Diet is unplanned and reactive — convenience eating because planning takes effort he has no capacity left for
Responsibility split across six commitments plus being a father, on top of a breakup one week earlier
Has repeatedly asked friends and trainer friends for help and been left hanging for a week or two at a time
Severe financial constraint — roughly $500 CAD monthly surplus, two maxed credit cards, no savings, about $100 in his account and outstanding debt
Self-doubt about staying committed and fear of wasting his own money and other people's time
Both parents in poor health from lifelong inactivity, and the men in his family die of heart attacks around the age he is approaching
Training alone at a gym is isolating and there is nobody present with him in the process

objections.raw_quote: until after Sundance, I'm not looking to start working out, really, like, I want to do the conditioning and focus my energy and time and energy on conditioning, like, just for now, and then when Sundance comes, after Sundance is when I'm looking to start doing strength stuff and doing kettlebell stuff
objections.rep_response: Reframed the imminent ceremony as a reason to start immediately rather than wait — 'especially with the Sundance come up, man, that's almost a reason to actually jump on board the kettlebells ASAP, because the amount of conditioning you can get just from a kettlebell is ridiculous' — and suggested he ask Trevor for programming aimed at that window.

objections.raw_quote: A bit of doubt. A bit of doubt in my own self... I sometimes have a difficult time staying committed to things. And I don't want to let that be the thing this time around.
objections.rep_response: Ran an uncertainty reframe — nobody knows with total certainty until they act — and split people into proactive committers versus reactive delayers, asking which gets further in life.

objections.raw_quote: I've never met Trevor. I don't know his energy. Are we actually gonna jive as people? Like, if I don't like the guy, I'm not gonna be able to work with him, right? Like, that's also a thing, right?
objections.rep_response: Never addressed. The rep did not respond to this at all and moved on to the commitment question and then the price.

objections.raw_quote: I think I do need to sleep on it, though, and just take some time to really sit with that. Because I need to see, like, well, is it worth it to me, right?
objections.rep_response: Isolated rather than rebutted — 'If I handed you a duffel bag full of cash that covered the cost of the investment, would you do it?' — then pushed past 'probably' to a definite yes, correctly establishing that the blocker was money and not conviction.

objections.raw_quote: I don't have it. I don't have 8,500 just sitting around. Okay. And like, like I'm in debt too. And like, I've been kind of just barely scraping it by for like a long time.
objections.rep_response: Took permission for an open financial conversation and ran the full financial picture — income, monthly expenses, surplus, credit availability, savings and cash on hand. Established roughly $500 CAD a month spare, two maxed cards totalling about $5,000 of limit, no savings and about $100 in his account. Concluded the programme and a payment plan were both out of reach and offered a $1,000 USD self-serve product instead, suggesting he save for a couple of months.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Raised but never structured. The rep said 'oftentimes we'll be able to break it up' and floated $500 a month, then judged it unworkable. He also said 'Oh, you're a Canadian. wouldn't work,' apparently ruling out some financing route on the basis of the prospect being outside the US, though the transcript is garbled at that point.

prospect_financials.note: Disclosed in Canadian dollars and converted here at the rate the rep used on the call (USD 6,000 = CAD 8,424). Originals: income roughly $1,600 CAD every two weeks; monthly expenses roughly $2,500-2,700 CAD including rent, insurance, phone, food and gas; roughly $500 CAD a month left over; about $100 CAD in his chequing account; two credit cards with limits of about $2,000 and $3,000, both completely maxed with nothing available; no savings and no investments; still paying down a family maintenance debt.

evidence: No payment taken, no verbal agreement to the programme and no payment link sent

The rep disqualified on affordability after running the financial picture: 'this could be a little tight on our end, because usually, like, oftentimes we'll be able to break it up. I think 500 a month' followed by the prospect's 'it's a little bit out of my reach'
The rep redirected to a different, cheaper product rather than closing: 'here's where I think we need to start... That's a thousand USD'
No follow-up call was booked; the close was an open-ended 'take a couple months, stack that up, and then just reach back out when you're ready'
The rep's sign-off reads as a goodbye: 'I'm sending some followers your way, man... I want to see that come through to fruition in the next year or so'

Counter-evidence for a follow_up reading: the prospect did not decline the $1,000 product, checked the conversion live and responded 'Sweet. Okay. Well, I appreciate it, man. Thank you.' He also rated the programme 8 out of 10 and confirmed commitment twice. The loss is affordability, not desire.
Counter-evidence: the prospect had said before the price was quoted that he wanted to sleep on it, so a decision was never going to land on this call regardless
outcome.next_step: Prospect to save toward the $1,000 self-serve product over a couple of months and reach back out; nothing scheduled.

notable.note: The most concerning call in this batch on clinical grounds and the clearest pricing deviation. The prospect disclosed generalised joint hypermobility with unstable knees, a vertebra displaced by a seven-foot fall onto concrete, daily headaches and crippling daily pain, and recurrent depressive and manic episodes. The rep asked the injury question, received all of it, and followed up on none of it. He then actively encouraged starting kettlebell conditioning immediately as preparation for Sundance — four to six hours of dancing daily for four days without food or water, beginning nine days after this call — with no clinician involved at any point. Separately, after a correctly run financial-picture play established the prospect had about $100 in his account, two maxed credit cards, no savings and roughly $500 CAD a month spare, the rep introduced a $1,000 USD self-serve product that is neither of the two sanctioned tiers. On the positive side, the discovery, root-cause work and money play were among the most complete in this batch, and the rep did stop rather than pushing an unaffordable close. One objection was ignored entirely: the prospect asked whether he and Trevor would get on, and received no answer. Note also that this prospect misses all five stated ICP criteria and still reached a 73-minute closer call.

quality.notes: Attribution inverts frequently and sometimes for long stretches. Clear instances: at 00:06:50 the prospect's Sundance explanation is split across both labels; at 00:29:46 the rep's 'Sounds like you're just looking for a bit of a system' is attributed to Ryan; at 00:45:31, 00:46:15 and 00:55:02 whole turns invert; at 01:04:37 and 01:09:20 the question-and-answer pairs are reversed. Role was read from content throughout. A long unpunctuated run from 00:01:40 to 00:05:03 has no timestamps or speaker boundaries at all. The transcript censors profanity heavily, which removes words mid-sentence, and mangles the financial figures around 01:08:14 where rent and expense numbers appear as '$5.50', '$3.50' and '$1.75' — the surrounding context makes the monthly totals recoverable but the individual line items are not reliable. One internet dropout at 00:57:07 lost roughly fifteen seconds of the rep's reframe.
